minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 1, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on July 1, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 26, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall, 200 Civic Center, at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and at the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way. A copy was also posted at Council
Member Ury’s remote location, the Embassy Suites Hotel, 550 Winter Street, Waltham, MA.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  Council Member Ury (present for a portion of the meeting from 7:30
  p.m. to 11:21 p.m. via conference call from Waltham, Massachusetts)

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk/Director of Community Relations

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation. Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: (One
  Case.)

City Council Minutes  1  July 1, 2013
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update on some litigation-
related matters but no reportable action occurred.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize The Friends of the Library for Having Raised over $2 Million Dollars for
  the Mission Viejo Library

  Mayor Reardon presented the certificate of appreciation to the Friends of the Mission Viejo
  Library.

P2. Legislative Advocacy Update

  The City Council received a presentation from Cori Williams, Associate with Townsend
  Public Affairs.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cal Hullihen, M.V.: introduced himself and his wife Marta, owners of the new Elements
Therapeutic Massage in Gateway Center. Mr. Hullihen thanked City staff and the Council for
attending their grand opening and he extended an invitation to visit their booth at the 4th of July
Street Faire.

Dan Avery, M.V.: thanked the Council for the median beautification along Marguerite Parkway
in front of the Civic Center.

Margo Ferron, Event Chair for Relay for Life and Donna Lang Stockle, Owner of Massage
Heights: announced that this year's Relay for Life raised $170,110 and they are competing to be
the #1 Relay of Orange County next year. They invited residents to the July 4th Street Faire
where they will be serving food, sponsored by Outback, with all profits going to the Relay.
Lastly, Ms. Ferron asked that Massage Heights be allowed to have a sign twirler and corner
signage on July 16 to help promote an American Cancer Society fundraiser.

Susan Sellers, M.V.: announced that the dog park fundraiser, the Bone Yard Bash, will be held
on July 13 from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. in the Kershaw Garden at the Civic Center. Mrs. Sellers
directed residents to www.cityofmissionviejo.org/dogpark to purchase tickets for the event or to
purchase a custom dog park paver and other items.

City Council Minutes  2  July 1, 2013
 Elizabeth Busick, M.V.: requested that the Council provide full funding for library programs and
books. She noted that 60% of Mission Viejo residents use the library which proves that the
facility effectively serves the population and there is no better "bang for your buck."

Gail Reavis, M.V.: shared a newspaper advertisement for an Aliso Viejo swimming pool which
is open to the public and collects fees for community usage. She recommended that any new
Nadadores contract include the allowance of public use for a fee.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he considers the Oso Creek Trail a crown jewel of
Mission Viejo and he enjoyed his recent participation in the monthly guided tour. He
recommended the placement of identifying signage near some of the plants and trees so residents
will know what they are.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: discussed the upcoming 4th of July Street Faire and she encouraged
residents to attend. Mrs. Bucknum wished Community Services Commissioner, Joyce Saltzgiver,
good luck with her upcoming surgery and she encouraged the community to come out and
support the Friends of the Dog Park by attending the Bone Yard Bash on July 13. She further
invited residents to attend the City's birthday event with the Pacific Symphony on July 27 and
she reminded the Council of the Nadadores Swim Meet of Champions which will bring a lot of
commerce to the City later this month.

Mary Lee Robinson, Vice President of the Oso Valley Greenbelt Association, M.V.: asked the
Council to consider extending the median islands on La Paz Road from Marguerite to Olympiad.
She asked that the project be kept on the CIP wish list and that the Council consider a modest
amount of funding for design.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 7, 11 and 26 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht and Reardon
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles

3.  Check Register Dated June 7, 2013 in the Amount of $460,018.68

City Council Minutes  3  July 1, 2013
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated June 14, 2013 in the amount of $739,555.24

City Council Minutes  4  July 1, 2013

City Council Minutes  5  July 1, 2013

20. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2013 - Phase 1

22. Adoption of the FY 2013-14 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 13-02 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community

23. Adoption of the FY 2013-14 Budget for the Mission Viejo Housing Authority

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 13-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo

24. Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2013-14 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 13-38 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2013-14 Fiscal

25. First Amendment to the Assistant City Manager Employment/Director of Public
  Services Employment Agreement

  Approved the attached First Amendment to the Assistant City Manager/Director of Public

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  6  July 1, 2013
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

37. Economic Development Committee Update

  Council Members Schlicht and Leckness presented the report.

Note: Council Member Ury joined the meeting at 7:30 p.m. via conference call from the
Embassy Suites hotel in Waltham, Massachusetts.

OLD BUSINESS

27. Adoption of the 2013-15 Budget

  Bob Breton, M.V.: outlined the Community Services Commission's prioritized list of

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-39 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2013-15 and
  Appropriating Funds for FY 13-14 Only; (2) defer the appropriation of $27,200 for public
  art on Crown Valley Parkway; (3) adopt Resolution 13-40 Updating the City's
  Classification System and Establishing Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications;
  and (4) add $472,000 for projects to be funded from the balance of discretionary funding as
  follows: security lighting at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center in the
  amount of $45,000, HVAC repairs at City Hall in the amount of $20,000, IT backup
  appliances in the amount of $95,000, Library materials in the amount of $62,000, plant
  materials in the amount of $50,000 and slope renovations in the amount of $200,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness, Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to defer the
  Marguerite Aquatics complex facility rehabilitation project (on the list of proposed projects

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury

  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  July 1, 2013
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to include the
  Pavion Park Universally Designed Playground Replacement in the park fees budget for
  Fiscal Year 13-14.
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to include the

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury

from the recess. Council Member Leckness returned at 9:33 p.m.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

26. Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  9  July 1, 2013
   Council Member Schlicht stated that she will vote no on the contract because she is
  concerned that Mr. Townsend has attempted to buy influence by donating to City Council

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff regarding the bid process, the lowest

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1) approve
  the contract to host the 2013 ITF Wheelchair Doubles Masters at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion

City Council Minutes  10  July 1, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

30. School Crossing Guard Services

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Baron Farwell, General Manager for All City Management Services, Santa Fe Springs:
  stated that All City Management (ACMS) can fulfill their responsibilities under the
  proposed contract however many of the crossing guards currently working for the City
  would not return next year, there will be a much higher turnover rate, the employees that do
  stay will be less than stellar, and the City will experience increased complaints. Mr. Farwell
  noted that each of these variables impacts the quality and safety of the Mission Viejo
  crossing guard program.

  Patricia Pohl, Director of Operations for All City Management Services, Lake Forest:
  announced that the level of service will change under the proposed contract with ACMS
  and that the current crossing guards will leave.

  The Council Members and City Attorney expressed great concern with Mr. Farwell's and
  Ms. Pohl's statements that the City will get less than stellar ACMS employees and that
  ACMS will provide defective service. Mr. Curley noted that he would need to add verbiage
  to the contract to protect the City.

  Lisa Harcrow, M.V.: attempted to clarify that her ACMS bosses did not mean to say that
  they would provide a lesser quality of service. Instead, they were trying to shake the
  Council up and make them realize that reducing the crossing guard pay will affect the
  appeal of the shift differential.

  Baron Farwell, General Manager for All City Management Services, Santa Fe Springs:
  outlined his response to the RFP and the turnover ratio when the crossing guard pay is
  reduced from 4 hours to 3 hours. He stated that the RFP didn't factor in the quality,
  commitment and integrity of the individual crossing guards.

  Carrie Payne, M.V.: stated that she has been a crossing guard for 22 years and has worked
  for ACMS for 20 years. She said that the City's contract dictates what the crossing guards
  will get paid and for a lot of the crossing guards, the $180 monthly pay cut will cause a
  hardship. Ms. Payne noted that she has come to love the children and families of Mission
  Viejo but she could not stay at her job if her pay is reduced to 3 hours a day.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to reject
  staff's recommendation and direct staff to come back with other proposals for Council
  consideration.

City Council Minutes  11  July 1, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

31. South Coast Air Quality Management District Funding for Electric Vehicle Charging
  Stations

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: encouraged the Council to move forward with the recommended
  action. He stated that the City has always taken a leading role in fostering energy
  conservation and employing methods to improve air quality.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1) approve the
  Agreement with the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) for funding
  for the design, equipment purchase, and installation of electric vehicle charging stations in
  Mission Viejo; and (2) adopt Resolution 13-XX Authorizing the City Manager to Serve as
  the Signatory Authority on Behalf of the City of Mission Viejo for all Contractual,
  Operational and Financial Capacities Related to Mobile Source Air Pollution Reduction
  Committee (MSRC) Projects.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Leckness
  NOES:  Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

Note: At the hour of 11:21 p.m., Council Member Ury left the meeting due to the late hour on

STAFF REPORTS

Mayor Reardon stated that the next step is to challenge the decision at the State level.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  14  July 1, 2013
 38. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness had nothing to report.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked the Mayor to close the meeting in memory of the 19 Granite
Mountain Hotshots who died tragically in the recent Arizona fires. She announced that she voted
against the budget for several reasons. First, she does not approve of the increase in staff salary
ranges after a 5% pay increase and she feels that the City is doing too much social spending at
the expense of infrastructure. Council Member Schlicht stated that the City is also starting to
compete more and more with the private sector and has not listened to the residents' opinions on
expenditure of $1 million for a dog park. She noted that the City created the budget but it's the
taxpayers that have to pay it and she thinks the Council could have done better. Council Member
Schlicht stated that she is looking forward to 6 weeks off and visiting with relatives and she
wished everyone a safe and sane 4th of July.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley expressed concern that the toll road extension challenge will have a huge
impact on Mission Viejo. She noted that all the residents to the east pass through this City to get
to and from the freeway and it is only going to get worse. She stated that she looks forward to
seeing what kind of work can be done with the problem. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined her
attendance at a recent Community of Character Committee meeting which focused on
formulating a program that would provide an ethics and character forum for 8th grade students.
She and Council Member Leckness met with a gentleman who manages a program like this in
Irvine and the committee decided to move forward with it. She described that students will meet
after school and will be presented with social and academic scenarios that they will discuss in
groups in order to come to an ethical character-driven solution. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reminded
everyone that the 4th of July Street Faire is this week and the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee does the lion's share of the work. The Activities Committee puts on quite a few
events each year and they are always in need of volunteers so she encouraged those who are
interested to contact her for more information or to look for MVAC on the Internet. Mayor Pro
Tem Kelly thanked Council Member Ury for giving up an evening of his vacation by calling in
to participate in tonight's meeting and sticking with it until 2:30 a.m. eastern time. Lastly, she
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of July is fairness.

City Council Minutes  15  July 1, 2013
 Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that the Coastal Commission staff has recommended that fire rings
remain in place and they will conduct a public hearing on the matter at the Ventura City Hall on
July 11 beginning at 8:30 a.m. Interested parties can stream the meeting live from the Coastal
Commission's website. Mayor Reardon discussed the public comments at the last Council
meeting concerning a resident's bad experience with a local business, Saatchi Jewelers. She read
from an email drafted by the City Attorney which notes that the Council cannot discuss or
disclose if or what the law enforcement agencies are undertaking in relation to this matter. She
announced that City staff has clear direction from the Council and will respond as directed
however, they must use caution and thoroughness to protect all parties. Mayor Reardon reminded
residents of the upcoming dog park fundraiser, the Bone Yard Bash, on July 13 beginning at 6:00
p.m. in the Kershaw Garden at the Civic Center. Tickets are $30 per person and can be purchased
on the City's website or at City Hall. She also announced that the Mission Viejo High School
Football team will pay homage to the military and they are seeking veterans and active military
men and women who would like to be honored at a football game on October 25, 2013. The
players will be wearing jerseys with the names of the military personnel and she advised anyone
who is interested to contact Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle for
more information. Mayor Reardon encouraged residents and her colleagues to attend the 4th of
July Street Faire and lastly, she invited Robert Breton to the podium to discuss resident Waldo
"Tex" Shannon who recently passed away.

Robert Breton, M.V.: echoed the Council Members’ comments about solving the corridor traffic
problems. Mr. Breton outlined Tex Shannon's contributions to the City of Mission Viejo and his
service to the Country during World War II.
